# First-source context

This is an informed local design study of the existing Qleisli declaration
paths. The author previously read the code, Reference, parameter/pattern studies
and their actual diagnostics; it is not a blind or controlled-model benchmark.
The exact deployed model identifier and sampling settings were unavailable.
No external model was invoked. The sources were authored before checking and
copied byte-for-byte from the frozen formal-access-candidate-01 packet into ten
independent complete projects. No source repair or parser/CLI/native run has
occurred in this preparation.

The production commit `6d95189960f78e51ea13db2ce85822b8ccabbd55` was previously
reported by root; no Git query or compiled-HEAD attestation was performed here.
The actual selected file identities, rather than that report, are guarded by
identity-prepared.json. Constitutional QS/PR/RS/EXACT obligations remain pending;
the two ordinary decoded QLV1 guarantees keep their existing restricted scope.
No new interpretation or guarantee is adopted.

The design note contains code-derived priority predictions, including sized
Basis availability before Natural normalization. None is an expected stdout or
acceptance oracle. The future collector records genuine whole-project finite
checks and complete selected preparation before checking closed main::main.
Unsupported early barriers do not test downstream generic kinds/access/bodies.
A valid closed main cannot rescue an invalid unused declaration. An ultimately
rejected project can have made earlier native calls.

Only check commands are prepared. There is no run/sample/emission, semantic
oracle, maximum/stress case, source-preservation proof, canonical std/QFT
integration, guarantee discharge, Issue completion or release claim.
